## Judgment

### Expected-drift set

`modules/core/security.nix` reaches every NixOS host through both profiles, so
disabling `services.gnome.gcr-ssh-agent` drifts all four.
`modules/tools/ssh-tpm-agent.nix` adds a systemd user session variable on
sweet16 and petunia only.

Expected: all four NixOS hosts drift; standalone groot HM configurations do
not move.

### Actual vs expected

Matches: sweet16, petunia, avina and hermes drift; groot@dualie and
groot@forge byte-identical; groot@rk3588 N/A (aarch64).

### The defect

`ssh-add -l` in a desktop terminal showed the old ed25519 keys, not the TPM
keys, while a login shell was correct. Three agents were in play:

  systemd user manager env : SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/run/user/1000/gcr/ssh  (no identities)
  the terminal's inherited  : /run/user/1000/gnupg/S.gpg-agent.ssh (two ed25519)
  login shell               : /run/user/1000/ssh-tpm-agent.sock    (correct)

Graphical terminals inherit from the systemd user manager, which reads only
`environment.d`. `home.sessionVariables` writes a profile.d snippet and so
never reaches them. gnome-keyring's gcr-ssh-agent was exporting SSH_AUTH_SOCK
into that environment and winning by default.

Both variables are now set deliberately, because they cover different entry
points: `home.sessionVariables` for login shells, `systemd.user.sessionVariables`
for anything the user manager spawns.

`services.gnome.gcr-ssh-agent.enable` is a dedicated option, so only the SSH
agent component is disabled; keyring credential storage is untouched.

### Verified before deploying

The generated `environment.d/10-home-manager.conf` carries
`SSH_AUTH_SOCK=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/ssh-tpm-agent.sock` alongside the existing
QT variables, and `services.gnome.gcr-ssh-agent.enable` evaluates false.

### Requires a session restart to observe

Neither change affects a running session: the user manager's environment is
fixed at start, and the pre-migration gpg-agent (running since 15:02) keeps
answering on its socket. A full logout is needed before a desktop terminal
picks up the TPM agent.
